research_rationale: EO 12985 (61 FR 1209, signed 1996-01-11) establishes the Armed Forces Service Medal. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12985.txt): section 1 establishes the medal for members who on or after June 1, 1992 take part in a significant U.S. military operation and meet no foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action; section 2 provides design approval and award by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation as to the Coast Guard, with precedence before the Humanitarian Service Medal; section 3 limits award to operations with no other service medal and allows one medal with devices; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text has no sunset, deadline or condition. Later instruments found in the held texts that cite the number: EO 13286 section 20 (signed 2003-02-28, effective 2003-03-01 under its section 92) replaces the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security in section 2; EO 13154 section 2 (2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (2003-03-12) each begin Notwithstanding section 3 of Executive Order 12985 and keep members who qualified through Kosovo service or terrorism-related operations qualified, while allowing the Kosovo Campaign Medal or the Global War on Terrorism medals in lieu. These are an amendment and exceptions, recorded as later events on sections 2 and 3; none revokes or supersedes a clause. The dossier's EO 12977 record carries EO 13286 section 23 text, and EO 12977 predates this order, so it is not an event.
